We are delighted to present TASNEE's Eighth (8 th ) Annual Sustainability Report, showcasing our Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) and Sustainability performance for 2024. This report highlights our continued commitment to driving sustainable growth, fostering transparency, and embracing global best practices, as we strive to create longterm value for our stakeholders. The report provides a comprehensive overview of our activities and performance across key ESG areas, including: -  Our environmental stewardship efforts, aimed at minimizing our footprint and promoting eco-friendly practices -  Our social responsibility initiatives, focused on enhancing the well-being of our employees, communities, and customers -  Our governance framework, designed to ensure accountability, transparency, and ethical business practices By sharing our progress and challenges, we demonstrate our dedication to sustainability, transparency and reaffirm our commitment to making a positive impact on the environment and on our society.
The report covers the calendar year from 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2024, unless stated otherwise.

Developed in accordance with the GRI Sustainability Reporting Standards (refer to Appendix B for the GRI Content Index), this report is also guided by key national and international sustainability frameworks, including the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs), Saudi Green Initiative (SGI), and Saudi Vision 2030.

The report encompasses all TASNEE-operated facilities in Saudi Arabia and covers its three Strategic Business Units (Petrochemicals, Downstream, and Metallurgy), alongside its Business Units. Unless explicitly stated, data related to external contractors, suppliers, and customers are not included.

We recognize the importance of stakeholder engagement in shaping our sustainability journey. We welcome feedback, insights, and recommendations to enhance our reporting and performance. Please direct any comments or inquiries to Chief ESG and Sustainability Officer (ESGS@TASNEE.COM).

Eng. Mubarak A. Al Khafrah Chairman On behalf of the Board of Directors and our valuable partners, I am honoured to present TASNEE's 2024 Annual Sustainability Report. This report reflects our continued commitment to integrating Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) and Sustainability across all aspects of our business, showcasing the tremendous progress we have made towards a more sustainable and resilient future. At TASNEE, sustainability is deeply embedded in our corporate culture and business operations. It is not just a strategic priority, but a fundamental aspect of our daily activities. Our newly launched ESG Strategy reinforces this commitment, and we are proud to have made significant strides in our performance, driving progress and excellence in ESG efforts. By integrating sustainable practices, we drive business growth, enhance operational efficiency, mitigate risks, and contribute to the Kingdom's ambitious objectives under Saudi Vision 2030. Our innovative ESG and Sustainability initiatives align with the global sustainability agenda, reinforcing our corporate goals and commitment to responsible business leadership, and robust governance. In 2024, we made significant headway in ESG and Sustainability stewardship. Our decarbonization roadmap continues to advance, leading to measurable reductions in greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across our operations. These strides are bolstered by our commitment to enhancing energy efficiency and minimizing waste, ensuring that we play a proactive role to address the global climate challenges. Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) remains central to our mission, as we strive to create lasting positive change in the communities we serve. Through increased investment in local community initiatives, we are fostering economic development, societal progress, and human capital growth reinforcing our alignment with Vision 2030. As we look to the future, our commitment to ESG and Sustainability remains unwavering. At TASNEE, we are dedicated to setting the standard for responsible business practices by embracing innovative technologies, championing sustainable solutions and driving meaningful change. Our goal is to build a resilient, inclusive, and forwardlooking enterprise that benefits our employees, customers, and stakeholders alike. With the establishment of our new dedicated ESG and Sustainability function, I am confident that TASNEE will achieve even greater heights of excellence and make a lasting and positive impact. I extend my heartfelt thanks to all TASNEE employees, partners, and stakeholders for their continued support and contributions. Our collective efforts make our achievements possible, and I look forward to continuing this journey together as we work toward a prosperous and sustainable future. I also pray for the continued health and success of our Kingdom's leadership under the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz AlSaud, Crown Prince and Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia .

At TASNEE, we prioritize Environment, Social, and Governance (ESG) and Sustainability, embedding these principles into our core business practices to drive responsible growth, innovation, and excellence. We strive to find better ways to provide the materials the world needs while driving innovation and continuous improvement. We aim to produce sustainable products, used daily, in the safest and most sustainable ways possible. This commitment extends beyond our products to the communities we serve, as we strive to create a better future for all. Our team is deeply committed to helping us achieve our sustainability ambitions and positively impact the communities in which we operate. In 2024, we made significant progress towards reducing our environmental footprint. Notably, our Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions intensity decreased more than 8% from the previous year across our organization, driven by improved energy efficiency and increased production throughput. This accomplishment is particularly remarkable given the ongoing expansion of our operations. Our commitment to circular economy principles also yielded significant results, with a substantial improvement in material loss intensity. We increased our waste recycling/reuse rate from 16.41 MT per metric ton of production in 2023 to 18.25 MT in 2024, representing an impressive 11% improvement in just one year . These achievements demonstrate our dedication to minimizing our environmental impact and promoting sustainable growth. Meanwhile, our digital transformation journey continues to propel us towards excellence in ESG and Sustainability. By harnessing innovative digital technologies - including 3D Printing, Artificial Intelligence, Circular Economy Solutions, and Drone Technology - we are significantly enhancing operational efficiency, strengthening governance, enhancing data-driven decision-making, and minimizing our environmental footprint. The successful integration of Robotic Process Automation (RPA) and other systems has further optimized processes, driven operational efficiency, and accelerated progress toward our sustainability objectives. The efforts and performance of our workforce are key to achieving these milestones. In 2024, we achieved a 27% increase in total training hours , reflecting our commitment to upskilling our employees and preparing them for the challenges ahead. These efforts are aligned with our digitalization initiatives, which enhance both the effectiveness of our workforce and our overall operational agility. As we continue to make progress on our ESG and Sustainability roadmap, we remain focused on achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2060. This goal is central to our strategy, and we are actively exploring renewable energy solutions, including solar installations and energy efficiency projects across our facilities. Our efforts are in line with Saudi Vision 2030, and we are committed to contributing to the Kingdom's economic diversification and sustainability objectives.

Alongside our environmental progress, we remain dedicated to fostering a culture of inclusion and development. This year, our workforce grew more diverse, with a particular focus on increasing opportunities for young talent and women. As we continue to expand and grow, we ensure that our people have the tools and support they need to thrive in a dynamic and sustainable business environment. I am proud of the progress we have made in 2024, but our journey is far from over. We will continue to lead by example, driving innovation, embracing new technologies, and working towards a sustainable future. I would like to extend my gratitude to all TASNEE employees, partners, and stakeholders for their invaluable contributions to this shared success. Together, we will continue to make meaningful strides towards a better, and more sustainable world. We offer thanks to Allah the almighty for his blessings and the steadfast leadership of the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and His Royal Highness Prince Mohammed bin Salman bin Abdulaziz Al-Saud, Crown Prince and Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia . Since inception in 1985, the National Industrialization Company (TASNEE) has played a crucial role in Saudi Arabia's industrial development, becoming the country's first fully owned joint-stock private-sector industrial company. Headquarters in Riyadh, TASNEE was founded to drive economic diversification, fostering innovation and technological advancement within the Kingdom's industrial and petrochemical sectors. Almost 40 years since inception, TASNEE, together with its entities and subsidiaries, has evolved into one of Saudi Arabia's largest and most influential industrial and petrochemical companies, with a significant global footprint in the Metallurgy sector (Titanium). Our reputation is built on a commitment to operational efficiency, advanced manufacturing, and sustainable innovation, enabling us to deliver high-performance products and services while continuously adopting cutting-edge technologies to meet evolving industry demands. TASNEE operates across multiple strategic sectors, including, petrochemicals, chemicals, downstream products, advanced metals to industrial services. The company is deeply involved in the development, management, and marketing of industrial projects, ensuring the integration of advanced industrial technology into Saudi Arabia's economy. Through its subsidiaries, TASNEE produces and distributes an extensive range of petrochemical products, such as ethylene, polyethylene, propylene, polypropylene, butyl acrylate, acrylic acid, super absorbent polymers, and butanol, alongside industrial materials, including ilmenite slag, titanium sponge, lead-acid car batteries, lead, high-performance plastic products, and acrylic sheets. Beyond production, TASNEE actively engages in technical services, equipment testing, and the operation of key industrial and energy facilities, including chemical, petrochemical, metallurgical, water desalination, and power generation plants. TASNEE's vision and mission serve as the foundation of our operations, shaping our approach to responsible business practices and long-term sustainability. Through robust policies, standard operating procedures (SOPs), strong governance, and strategic initiatives, we translate our commitment into actions. We uphold the highest standards of quality, health, safety, and security, minimizing our environmental impacts, and fostering strong principles of ESG and Sustainability across our value chain. By embedding these principles into every aspect of our business, we create lasting value for our stakeholders and communities, reinforcing our role as a responsible and forward-thinking industry leader.

We are actively reducing emissions across our operations by optimizing performance, enhancing energy efficiency, and implementing clean and renewable energy solutions. Our decarbonization roadmap, aligned with Saudi Vision 2030 and the Saudi Green Initiative (SGI), outlines a strategic pathway to achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2060 across our Strategic Business Units (SBUs), utilizing the latest technologies and sustainable energy solutions. As part of our strategy, we conducted a baseline emissions audit, revealing that 71% of our total annual emissions are from direct (Scope 1) sources, which include fuel gas consumption, fuel oil consumption (if any), companyowned vehicles, process emissions such as flaring, fugitive emissions, and point source emissions. The remaining 29% are indirect emissions (Scope 2) from purchased energy. To address this, we are advancing a hybrid approach that prioritizes future adoption of hydrogen refueling, postcombustion carbon capture, and continuous improvement in plant reliability. Additionally, we are proceeding with the solar power systems at T&I site to cover 25% of energy requirement, while other site offices' power needs evaluation is ongoing, with a targeted total reduction of 4,747 MT CO2e emissions. TASNEE has developed a comprehensive decarbonization roadmap, quantifying Scope 1 and Scope 2 carbon emissions across all TASNEE operations for each activity, product, and service. This initiative, led jointly by TASNEE Petrochemical SBU and the T&I teams, enables precise tracking of carbon emissions at every stage of operations. Moving forward, T&I will focus on exploring innovative and emerging decarbonization technologies, while Petrochemical SBU will implement decarbonization initiatives through Management of Change (MOC), a systematic approach to managing organizational change, and projects to achieve roadmap targets and reduce emissions. As part of this commitment, TASNEE is implementing various initiatives aimed at reducing 117,000 MT CO2 e emissions within the petrochemical sector by 2030. We have adopted a phased decarbonization strategy (20252060), allowing for financial flexibility while adapting to evolving policies, technological advancements, and market dynamics. A key planned initiative focuses on phasing out the use of heavier liquid fuels, replacing them with methane to enhance efficiency and lower emissions. We also actively collaborate with external partners and licensors to integrate cutting-edge decarbonization technologies, ensuring alignment with global sustainability standards. We commenced our decarbonization journey in 2024.

Our strategy also defines our vision for a decarbonized future state and includes comprehensive scenario planning as part of our ongoing strategic development. We are in the process of finalizing a roadmap and implementation plan, with specific focus on developing carbon capture initiatives pending approval. Our efforts to operationalize decarbonization are actively progressing, demonstrating our commitment to a sustainable future. Access to clean and fresh water is a fundamental human right as outlined in the UN SDG's. However, in many regions, including our own, water scarcity continues to pose water stress challenges for people, businesses, and the environment. As climate change intensifies, the responsible and efficient use of water is more critical than ever to mitigate depletion and prevent pollution. TASNEE has a comprehensive water management approach aimed at minimizing freshwater consumption, optimizing water efficiency, mitigating water stress and ensuring wastewater treatment compliance with regulatory requirements. At PetChem, approximately 99% of the water supply is seawater used for cooling, sourced from a third party. PetChem employs a closed-loop cooling system and pretreats wastewater before sending it to an external facility, integrating advanced technologies to enhance efficiency and sustainability. PetChem has actively enhanced its water management practices as an integral component of its sustainability program. A significant achievement in this initiative was the repair of a ruptured Glass Reinforced Plastic (GRP) header in the cooling water loop. This fix significantly enhanced the reliability of water systems throughout the complex. PetChem manages, monitors and analyzes water consumption across its operations effectively. This is achieved through flow transmitters (FT) installed on every line, allowing us to accurately measure water consumption and usage distribution. This process helps PetChem identify opportunities to increase efficiency and promote sustainable water use. Additionally, PetChem fosters a culture of water conservation within its workforce by distributing educational flyers that emphasize the importance of water conservation and encourage all employees to adopt these practices. PetChem routinely assesses the condition of steam traps, replacing any defective units. This not only ensures the efficiency of steam trap systems but also aligns with the overarching objective of sustainable water management. Regular evaluations and upgradation of steam traps further improve system efficiency. Moreover, PetChem has optimized the operation of its seawater pumps, adjusting them to run only as needed, which has greatly reduced seawater intake. These thorough and deliberate efforts showcase PetChem's strong commitment to sustainable water management and resource optimization. content_text: At TASNEE, the health and safety of our employees and contractors is our top priority. We are committed to fostering a strong safety culture across all our operations, ensuring that stringent safety standards and requirements are met at every level. Our robust Environment, Health, Safety, and Security (EHSS) strategy includes preventative policies, procedures, and emergency preparedness guidelines, designed to mitigate risks and enhance workplace safety. In the event of a health and safety-related incident, we have thorough response protocols in place, ensuring immediate action, detailed investigations, and root cause analysis. These measures allow us to identify key learning points and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence. TASNEE is a proud member of the global Responsible Care ® initiative, aligning with a shared vision for environmental, health, and safety excellence. We also maintain ISO45001:2018 certification for Occupational Health and Safety Management, which guides our processes and protocols to uphold a safe and compliant working environment. By continuously strengthening our safety measures and enhancing our EHSS framework, we strive to maintain a zero-harm workplace, ensuring the wellbeing of our people while driving operational excellence.

TASNEE's Journey Toward EHSS Excellence program is a structured initiative aimed at enhancing EHSS performance and ensuring compliance with industry best practices. The program provides a comprehensive assessment of our safety framework, allowing us to identify strengths, address gaps, and implement targeted improvements at all SBU's, BU's and cascading down to the department level. By fostering a proactive safety culture, we continuously refine our processes to mitigate risks and drive operational excellence. As part of this initiative, PetChem has established 143 KPIs, systematically monitored on a monthly basis to track compliance and progress. Regular EHSS audits ensure that corrective actions are effectively implemented, reinforcing our commitment to continuous improvement. The KPIs are categorized into five main groups with 18 subcategories. This enables a comprehensive, data-driven approach to EHSS performance management, as illustrated here.

TASNEE's EHSS Steering Committee convenes quarterly, bringing together both management and non-management representatives to ensure diverse perspectives are reflected in decision-making. The Committee plays a critical role in driving EHSS improvements, offering recommendations to enhance existing systems and practices while ensuring alignment with industry standards and regulatory requirements. Key responsibilities include reviewing EHSS-related KPIs, monitoring plant performance, assessing incident reports, and overseeing safety campaigns. The Committee also identifies workplace challenges, explores potential risks, and proposes practical solutions to strengthen EHSS performance across all operations. Through this collaborative approach, TASNEE reinforces its commitment to a safe, compliant, and continuously improving work environment. A CULTURE OF CARE

At TASNEE, we believe that a healthy workforce is a more productive and engaged workforce. When employees experience high levels of well-being, they are less likely to be absent due to illness making them better equipped to contribute positively to our overall success To support this, we have established comprehensive policies, frameworks, and procedures based on internationally recognized risk management standards, helping to mitigate potential health risks while investing in proactive well-being initiatives. TASNEE offers comprehensive Occupational Health (OH) Surveillance and Preventive Medical programs designed to promote employee health and well-being. The program includes the following: -  Pre-employment medical examinations -  Periodic medical examinations -  Specialized medical assessments -  Pulmonary protection program -  Immunization program -  Food handling program -  Health promotion initiatives The programs are audited and certified by an independent third party to ensure we adhere to the best practices and regulatory requirements.

Employees actively contribute to the development, implementation, and evaluation of the company's occupational health and safety management system. They provide safety recommendations, nominate training programs, and assess the effectiveness of training sessions. We also conduct an annual safety committee meeting, involving worker participation. This meeting serves as a platform to discuss workplace safety challenges and improvements. To further support employee health, we provide an on-site clinic for first aid and initial medical treatment. If additional care is required, employees are referred to external medical facilities, with coverage provided through a contracted insurance provider across the Kingdom. Our Healthy Day program offers blood pressure monitoring, blood sugar testing, weight monitoring, hearing assessments, and health education sessions, ensuring employees have access to preventive healthcare and medical guidance. Employee medical records are securely maintained and can only be accessed by authorized medical personnel. 100% of employees have been covered under a certified health and safety management system, verified through external audits for the past three years In 2024, PetChem achieved a major milestone, meeting the stretch target of Process Safety Incident Severity rate, marking a significant advancement in EHSS standards.

The Lost-Time Injury Frequency Rate (LTIFR) for employees in 2024 was zero - a significant improvement from previous year 2023 records which was 2. Similarly, the Contractor LTIFR decreased in 2024 from 4.102 to 0.79 in comparison with the previous year. The Total Recordable Injury Frequency Rate (TRIFR) for employees dropped from 2.76 in 2023 to 0.35 in 2024, while the contractor TRIFR improved from 3.74 to 2.68 over the same period. These reductions reflect TASNEE's continued efforts to enhance workplace safety and minimize incidents. All reported incidents were thoroughly investigated, and corrective actions were implemented to prevent recurrence. We are focused on rigorous safety oversight and compliance; the total number of Health, Safety, Environment, and Security (HSE&S) audits for contractors increased from 251 in 2023 to 280 in 2024. Importantly, over the past three years, TASNEE has reported no work-related fatalities, demonstrating the effectiveness of our health and safety performance protocols. In 2024, TASNEE delivered a total of 4,477 hours of comprehensive health and safety training to both employees and contractors. These training hours ensure employees and contractors are equipped with the necessary knowledge to maintain a safe working environment. Notably, contractor health and safety training hours increased from 1,111 hours to 1,417 hours in 2024 from the previous year, representing a 27.5% growth, strengthening contractor safety awareness and compliance. 1,417 safety training hours in 2024 In 2024, AMIC Toho Titanium Metal Company Ltd. (ATTM), a joint venture between Advanced Metal Industries Cluster Company Ltd. (AMIC) and Toho Titanium Company, achieved significant milestones in safety enhancement and regulatory compliance. All mandatory training sessions were successfully conducted for site stakeholders, ensuring adherence to the highest safety standards. The training programs covered fire watch, gas detection, firefighting, permit-to-work, the Lockout-Tagout (LOTO) system, first aid, and confined space entry, among others. These sessions have been instrumental in strengthening the Safety Management System (SMS), leading to improvements in the Total Recordable Incident Rate (TRIR) and overall EHSS performance. The year concluded on a strong note, meeting our stretched TRIR target and zero process safety incidents were reported. Additionally, HCIS compliance saw notable progress, marked by the installation of 22 additional CCTV cameras and also HCIS has approved our new EHSS structure.

As part of efforts to foster a proactive safety culture, ATTM introduced the Best Employee of the Month Award initiative in 2024. This program aims to recognize and reward employees who demonstrate exceptional contributions to safety, health, or environmental improvements. Each month, three awards - one for each process area - are presented to employees with the most impactful ideas or initiatives. The program has strengthened collaboration, innovation, and employee engagement, encouraging a more safety-conscious work environment. Looking ahead, the department is committed to sustaining and expanding this practice to further embed a culture of safety, recognition, and continuous improvement. 2M safe manhours worked without lost time injury by Metallurgy SBU achieving their safety goal

At TASNEE, we recognize that health and well-being are fundamental to workplace safety. Our well-being approach focuses on both shortand long-term preventive measures, ensuring employees have access to the resources they need to maintain their health. Employees are actively encouraged to participate in annual health screenings, which play a critical role in the early detection of potential health issues and provide guidance on necessary support. 1,301 health screenings completed in 2024

Promoting employee well-being goes beyond just safety; it involves creating an environment that supports active and healthy lifestyles. TASNEE organizes awareness campaigns focused on key health issues, empowering employees to make more informed and healthier choices. All employees are eligible for annual health screenings, and in 2024, we completed 1,301 screenings - a 6% increase from 2023.

With respect to Saudi Arabia's extreme summer temperatures, heat stress is a critical workplace concern. TASNEE proactively integrates heat stress mitigation into risk assessments, implementing precautionary measures that have resulted in a steady decline in heat-related cases year after year. During the summer months, we enhance our efforts through targeted awareness programs and specialized training, educating workers on the causes, risks, and treatment of heat stress. Our comprehensive approach has proven highly effective, and for three consecutive years, we have recorded zero heat stress cases, underscoring our dedication to employee safety and well-being.

At TASNEE, for all its sites, we ensure the availability of critical resources and well-defined procedures for effectively responding to potential incidents such as spills, leaks, fires, explosions and natural disasters. These emergency response protocols are regularly tested through mock drills for each respective scenario, with employees trained and continuously updated on emergency management techniques. We also invest in cuttingedge technologies to enhance our emergency response capabilities, ensuring we remain prepared for any situation. In 2024, TASNEE conducted 59 emergency response drills across its SBUs, marking a 34% increase from 2023. This improvement reflects our ongoing commitment to preparedness, maintaining high safety standards, and proactively identifying and addressing system vulnerabilities. Across all business units, emergency response drills increased significantly. For instance: Downstream drills increased from 21 to 36, while AMIC drills rose from 16 to 17 in reporting year 2024 compared to the previous year. We remain an active member of JAMA'A, which provides specialized training and emergency response exercises. In 2023, PetChem achieved a 100% score in JAMA'A's annual drill evaluation. Looking ahead, we will continue enhancing our emergency preparedness initiatives, ensuring swift, effective responses to any potential incidents while prioritizing the safety of our employees and operations. We continuously monitor asset performance and business operations, conducting regular inspections, equipment testing, and sound engineering assessments, all underpinned by a robust risk management framework. By proactively identifying potential vulnerabilities, we ensure the reliability, efficiency, and safety of our operations. Across our sites, we systematically identify, manage, and mitigate both internal and external risks, including: Recurring process safety incidents resulting from non-compliance with Process Safety Management System requirements or ineffective system implementation. Workplace safety challenges and risks to the integrity of operating systems and processes that handle hazardous substances. To mitigate these risks, we operate an integrated risk identification and mitigation system mapping emerging trends, enabling us to preemptively limit or eliminate potential disruptions. This proactive approach enhances operational excellence, improves productivity, and reinforces workplace safety. Our comprehensive risk management practices cover health, fire prevention, security, safety, and environmental protection across all project phases - from planning and construction to daily operations. We regularly review and update our management systems in response to regulatory changes, operational developments, and evolving industry standards. Additionally, we conduct formal risk analysis and risk revalidation studies every five years, ensuring our systems remain current, effective, and aligned with best practices. TASNEE's asset management strategy is built on a comprehensive life cycle program, designed to ensure long-term reliability, efficiency, and sustainability of physical assets. This approach aligns with stakeholder objectives, translating corporate growth aspirations into actionable, plant-level goals through strategic asset management objectives. By integrating asset management activities, we have created a cohesive and cost-effective framework that optimizes the entire asset life cycle. This fosters transparent decision-making, effective information management, and operational resilience. Recognizing its critical role in sustaining performance, our asset management framework aligns with ISO 55001, a globally recognized standard for asset management excellence. Ranked just behind quality management in its influence, ISO 55001 plays a pivotal role in ensuring the long-term efficiency and reliability of our operations.

content_text: Our people are TASNEE's most valuable asset. At TASNEE, we are committed to providing a workplace where every employee can reach their full potential. By prioritizing talent development and training, we continue to attract, retain, and empower top talent, ensuring that as our people grow, so does our company's success.

We place strong emphasis on preparing young professionals for their future careers through a range of early career support initiatives. In 2024, our youth development programs enrolled 28 trainees, including the Youth Development Program, Saudi Early Engineers Development Program, TASNEE Development Program for Operators and Technicians in Jubail, and the Downstream Graduate Engineering Development Program. We also launched the Tatwar Training Program, designed to develop young Saudi talent by equipping them with essential 'soft skills' for professional growth. These initiatives run alongside a cognitive educational series that integrates on-the-job skills and competency training. We also support young leaders and female workforce empowerment through Saudization programs facilitated by the Ministry of Human Resources and the Human Resources Development Fund (HADAF). TASNEE's Leadership Competency Model defines the skills, behaviors, and attributes essential for effective leadership. This model serves as a strategic framework for leadership development, recruitment, performance evaluation, and succession planning, ensuring the long-term sustainability of TASNEE's leadership pipeline. We continue to drive digital transformation in HR, implementing key initiatives such as the FM (Facility Management) Ticketing System, Robotics Solutions for Mobile Billing Verification within Payroll Systems, and a new Attendance System. In addition, we successfully introduced our E-Curricula Program, offering a flexible, customizable suite of eight online learning tracks to promote structured career growth, self-directed learning, and 'learning on-the-go.' In 2024, TASNEE reinforced its commitment to excellence and innovation by participating in the prestigious Top Employers Certification Program, successfully completing a detailed survey covering over 300 HR practices. Additionally, we finalized the Internal Capabilities Program to introduce structured tracks for internal trainers, content creation, knowledge sharing, and youth training. A strong focus on youth development continued in 2024, with expanded training programs and increased intake. Further advancements included the successful completion of the SuccessFactor (SF) H2 upgrade and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) for The Advanced Smelting Industries Company (ASIC) HR businesses, alongside the smooth rollout of ASIC employees. These achievements reflect TASNEE's dedication to fostering a dynamic, forward-thinking HR function that empowers its workforce, strengthens governance, and drives digital transformation. In 2024, TASNEE's commitment to workforce development resulted in a 27% increase in total training hours, reaching 132,648 hours in totality. Employees received an average of 42 training hours each. A significant increase in training participation was observed across all employee levels and demographics. Training hours for male employees have raised to 129,586, and female employees received 3,062 hours of training, marking a substantial improvement from 2023. Additionally, it's more than doubled for executive and senior leadership training, reaching 836 hours, while middle management and staff training increased to 19,777 and 112,035 hours, respectively.

Despite the increase in training hours, the total cost of training decreased to SAR 4.6 million for the reporting year, compared to SAR 6.08 million in 2023. This cost reduction was achieved by leveraging digital learning platforms and shifting towards online and on the job training, making professional development more accessible and cost-efficient. In 2024, we enhanced our robust Learning and Development Framework by introducing and aligning programs to sustain, upskill, and reskill our workforce effectively. Such initiatives included the launch of the TASNEE 8 Development Programs, a structured learning framework consisting of eight levels tailored for different job levels. Each program offered employees relevant training to help them develop key skills and support their career growth. Additionally, we organized a Learning Week, introducing six public training sessions conducted both face-to-face at the HQ and virtually, with a total attendance of 2,668. Furthermore, we implemented the Tatwar Training Program specifically for young employees, offering five courses to equip them with skills and knowledge, facilitating a smooth transition into the workplace. 88% of our employees received performance and career reviews

To drive continuous improvement, TASNEE fosters a workplace culture that respects diversity, encourages self-accountability, and promotes a strong learning mindset. Training and development initiatives are a key component of our talent attraction and retention strategy, ensuring that employees have the skills and knowledge to operate safely and efficiently. Our market position remains strong. We regularly review our total reward strategies to remain competitive. Our culture defines our strength, and we have implemented proactive recruitment methods, including recruitment marketing and talent pooling, to attract top talent. We have also enhanced critical skills acquisition strategies and streamlined recruitment processes to accelerate hiring while maintaining a focus on candidate quality and long-term fit. In alignment with Saudi Vision 2030, we prioritize the recruitment and development of young professionals. In 2024, 496 employees at TASNEE were under the age of 30, accounting for 15.4% of the total workforce. While this reflects a slight decrease from 19.4% in 2023, TASNEE remains committed to fostering young talent. Out of 476 new hires in 2024, 49% were under 30, reinforcing our commitment to investing in the next generation of professionals. Additionally, female hires increased to 58, representing an 18% rise from the previous year, highlighting our efforts to enhance workforce diversity and inclusion. 15.4% of the total workforce at TASNEE were under the age of 30

In 2025, we will continue leveraging our succession planning program and leadership development framework, ensuring focused commitment to developing our leadership pipeline to cultivate high-potential leaders, thereby strengthening our talent pipeline and ensuring organizational readiness for future challenges.

At TASNEE, our goal is to create a workplace where every employee feels valued, engaged, and fulfilled. We believe that a highly engaged workforce drives productivity, innovation, and long-term success. Central to this is fostering a culture of respect, transparency, and open communication where employees' ideas, concerns, and feedback are actively heard and addressed. Through structured feedback mechanisms and performance reviews, employees can identify strengths, explore development opportunities, and set meaningful career goals. To enhance employee engagement, we conducted HR Week sessions to educate employees on HR policies and provide a platform for inquiries and career advice. This included management sessions for various role levels. We also conducted satisfaction surveys, held Townhall sessions for employee connection and feedback, and utilized programs like Fikrah in Petrochemical SBU for idea submissions on sustainability and operational efficiency. Also, we sustained the systematic approach to gathering feedback from newly hired employees through onboarding and engagement surveys, thereby ensuring a comprehensive understanding of and enhancing their early-stage experience. TASNEE fosters a continuous learning culture and promotes a dynamic learning environment through its Internal Capability Program. This program encourages diverse learning opportunities by inviting TASNEE employees to share their knowledge and showcase their talents through four paths: the Internal Trainer Path, where employees create and lead the training sessions; the Content Creation Path, where employees develop training materials and resources in collaboration with the Internal Trainer; the Sharing Knowledge Path, where employees present on specialized topics across large group; and the Youth Internal Trainer Path, where young employees develop their training skills and lead the sessions. Additionally, TASNEE continues with its endeavor in investing in technology and automation to be at the forefront of leading companies in the industry. In 2024 TASNEE successfully redesigned and digitized more than 30 HR processes in the automated system SAP SuccessFactors, which in turn led to increased utilization of company resources, efficiency of operations and a significant reduction in cost. With the continued success of our initiatives in 2024 which focused on developing, training, and empowering our employees through the process of continuous performance management. The HR department will continue to support TASNEE to achieve its strategies, goals and objectives and continue its efforts to continuously improve its processes, policies, and procedures, be pro-active in embracing change and overcoming challenges to increase efficiency, productivity and professional satisfaction to the future proofing our human capital. In 2024, we started our first participation in the 'Top Employers Certification program' through one of the world's most prestigious bodies, believing in promoting the value of 'excellence' in TASNEE and our confidence in the evolution of our HR practices to the extent that such a program testifies to the competitive advantages offered to our employees.

We provide employees with a comprehensive range of benefits designed to support staff retention and enhance workforce well-being. We also offer WalaPlus (branded as Testahel at TASNEE), a discount and benefits program tailored for employees and their families. The program operates across a network of more than 5,000 retail locations, and features an online discount portal, regularly updated promotional offers, and exclusive vouchers. TASNEE also offers a defined contribution plan, allowing eligible employees to save for their future with companymatched contributions, reinforcing our commitment to long-term financial security for our workforce. To further support work-life balance, we have streamlined access to parental leave through our HR system. In 2024, a total of 178 employees took parental leave, including 173 male and 5 female employees. TASNEE achieved a 100% return-to-work rate, with all employees resuming their roles after leave. Additionally, 172 employees (167 male and 5 female) remained employed 12 months after their return, reflecting a 97% parental leave retention rate.

A diverse workforce strengthens an organization, bringing a variety of perspectives, ideas, and experiences that better reflect the diverse nature of our customers and markets. At TASNEE, we are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace and have focused our diversity efforts on gender and broader representation. While we recognize that there is still more to achieve, we are proud of our progress and remain dedicated to building an equitable work environment. Our commitment to workplace equality is reflected in two key policies: the Equal Employment Opportunity Policy and the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) Policy, both of which reinforce our belief in respect, inclusion, and fairness for all employees. We maintain a zero-tolerance approach to harassment and discrimination. All allegations are taken seriously, thoroughly investigated, and addressed through due process. We are also committed to upholding and respecting human rights across all operations. Every employee is required to adhere to our Code of Conduct, which includes clear commitments to fairness, equality, and human rights principles. In alignment with Saudi Vision 2030, TASNEE continues to increase female representation in the workforce by adopting women-friendly policies and creating professional development opportunities. In 2024, the number of female employees increased by 63%, with 13 women now holding middle management positions, up from 8 in 2023. Additionally, we have introduced initiatives such as the E-Curricula Program, leadership training, and mentorship programs to empower female employees, enhance their career growth, and enrich their workplace experience.

TASNEE strives to be a profitable, growing, and sustainable company, committed to maintaining competitiveness and consistently delivering on our commitments to stakeholders. More than 59% of our revenue is generated within the Kingdom, with an additional 18% coming from the wider Middle East region. To ensure ongoing profitability, while minimizing our environmental impact, and achieving financial results that surpass stakeholder expectations, we continuously innovate by implementing operational improvements and cost efficiencies. This allows us to remain competitive in an ever evolving market while maintaining a strong and sustainable presence across the regions we serve. In 2024, TASNEE demonstrated strong growth and expansion, with several key financial indicators showing positive trends. Revenues increased from SAR 3.57 billion in 2023 to SAR 3.90 billion in 2024, reflecting improved market performance and higher sales. Total assets grew from SAR 25.38 billion to SAR 26.38 billion, highlighting TASNEE's continued investment in business expansion and operational capacity. National Batteries Company (NBC) launched a high-impact marketing campaign, driving 27% YoY sales growth. Meanwhile, Rasass Company introduced a new high-calcium alloy, securing global approvals and preparing for an expansion by 2027. Further global market expansion saw the titanium sponge plant (ATTM) secure partnerships in India and South Korea, progressing in its qualification process with European aerospace manufacturers. Meanwhile, the ASIC sales unit contributed to revenue growth by increasing titanium slag and pig iron exports to Italy, Egypt, and India, while prioritizing local supply to strengthen Saudi Arabia's industrial sector. Moving forward, TASNEE remains focused on expanding its customer base, optimizing operations, and enhancing economic value in 2025 and beyond.

Ethics and responsible business practices are foundational to maintaining the highest levels of compliance and professional integrity at TASNEE. We have established a comprehensive framework of structures and policies to ensure strict adherence to all applicable legal, regulatory, international standards, rules, and best practices across the company. Our goal is to foster a culture of transparency, honesty, and trust within our workforce and among all stakeholders, ensuring that we always operate responsibly and ethically. To achieve this, our compliance procedures are meticulously aligned with both internal and external requirements. These procedures are continuously reviewed and updated, ensuring that they remain relevant, effective, and in line with evolving industry standards and regulatory changes. incidents of non-compliance recorded at TASNEE for the third consecutive year TASNEE recorded zero incidents of non-compliance with our Code of Conduct and Business Ethics for the third consecutive year.

TASNEE regularly conducts risk assessment workshops to evaluate and address various risks within our operations. Commonly identified risks include conflict of interest, bribery and gifts, and inadequate management oversight. To mitigate these risks, we have implemented several preventive measures, including the adoption of a comprehensive AntiCorruption and Bribery Policy as well as an Antitrust and Competition Policy. Anti-corruption principles are deeply embedded in our Code of Conduct, and we consistently communicate our expectations and requirements to all employees. Our policies and systems are clearly defined and regularly updated to ensure compliance with Saudi law, which imposes penalties ranging from fines to imprisonment for violations. In 2024, 85% of our employees completed online training on anti-corruption practices, strengthening our collective commitment to ethical business conduct. Additionally, 100% of our operations underwent corruption-related risk assessments, ensuring that all areas of the business are fully aligned with our ethical standards. Notably, no incidents of corruption or fines occurred during the year, further reflecting our strong compliance culture. For the past three years, all TASNEE employees, including top management, middle management, and staff, have been receiving training of the organization's anti-corruption policies and procedures.

TASNEE's Code of Business Conduct is the cornerstone of our business culture, reflecting our unwavering commitment to integrity and ethical behavior across all operations. This Code applies to all TASNEE employees, management, and directors, and it is regularly communicated through emails, mandatory online training, in-person sessions, and annual disclosures. It is readily accessible to all employees via our intranet, ensuring consistent awareness and application. The Code establishes clear guidelines for the behavior we expect from all employees and reinforces our core values: Excellence, Integrity, Seeking Knowledge, and Teamwork. It also emphasizes our commitment to fair and transparent business practices, the well-being of our employees, and the importance of fostering long-term partnerships with the communities where we operate. The Code serves as a guide for everyone associated with TASNEE, empowering them to conduct business with integrity, accountability, and transparency. TASNEE works closely with stakeholders to ensure they are informed about regulatory developments and best practices, helping them maintain a broader perspective and stay compliant in their respective operations. For three consecutive years, TASNEE has not received any regulatory complaints, further validating our commitment to ethical conduct and compliance.

TASNEE is committed to fostering a safe and respectful work environment, which includes offering employees effective mechanisms to raise concerns. Our Whistleblowing Grievance and Non-Retaliation Policy ensures that employees can report grievances or noncompliance issues safely and confidentially. Multiple confidential communication channels, such as telephone and online platforms, are available to employees, and they are encouraged and trained to use these channels for reporting concerns. To protect whistleblowers, we offer guaranteed protection against retaliation for anyone reporting issues in good faith. All reports are treated seriously, and we ensure that violations of the law are reported within 24 hours. We also ensure that all incidents and reports are investigated respectfully, confidentially, and fairly. Under our Code of Conduct, all employees are expected to cooperate honestly and truthfully in any investigation, supporting the company's commitment to maintaining an ethical and compliant workplace.

Effective risk management is essential to TASNEE's long-term success, ensuring resilience in a changing business environment. Operating in the petrochemical and chemical industries, TASNEE addresses challenges such as geopolitical shifts and inflationary pressures while capitalizing on growth opportunities. Our risk management framework follows the best international practices, including ISO 31000:2018 and CMA guidelines, ensuring a structured approach to managing operational, financial, and market risks. TASNEE operates in a highly competitive global market, necessitating continuous risk analysis at all management levels. We combine qualitative and quantitative assessments to implement effective policies while ensuring compliance with regulations. The Board Risk and Governance Committee (RiskCom) provides oversight of risk issues across the company, focusing on governance, compliance, and risk mitigation. RiskCom oversees the development and implementation of TASNEE's ESG Framework and Policy guiding the company's ESG strategy, commitments, and key areas of focus, reporting its findings directly to the Board. The Committee also receives periodic updates from management on TASNEE's ESG framework, policy, and performance. To strengthen risk resilience, TASNEE's Corporate Risk Management Team ensures enterprise risk management, governance, and compliance across departments, supporting risk identification and response planning. We maintain a business continuity program, ensuring safety and uninterrupted service delivery during crises. In 2024, TASNEE mitigated feedstock price fluctuations through performance improvements and expenditure rationalization, using hedging strategies to manage financial risks. TASNEE also continuously monitors regulatory changes to ensure compliance with evolving laws, and enhances the governance guidelines to keep up with new requirements and strengthens compliance among suppliers and stakeholders. In 2024, we updated the Master Authority Schedule to streamline decision-making and implemented the Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL), reinforcing data security and compliance. A key achievement in digital risk management was the implementation of a new Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) system, developed with the cybersecurity team, set to be fully operational in 2025. Looking forward, TASNEE remains focused on proactive risk mitigation, governance improvements, and regulatory compliance to ensure longterm sustainability and resilience. Our corporate risk management, compliance and governance system has been established to serve the interests of our stakeholders, as well as to enable us to monitor our business's performance and successfully accomplish our goals and objectives. In our opinion and past trends, successful businesses are built on excellent risk management. TASNEE has implemented a strong risk management, governance & compliance strategy that has recently experienced rapid growth and maturity. To further enhance our efforts on risk management, compliance and governance in 2025, we will continue to: Enhanced GRC systems for effective and efficient management of risk, governance and compliance Concentrate on risk management, ethics, data management & data privacy compliance
Conduct workshops, training sessions, testing of the business continuity plans, and PDPL compliance Development of young individuals under the Youth Development Plan (YDP)

The Internal Audit Department aims to enhance and safeguard organizational value by providing risk-based, independent, and objective assurance, advice, and insights. We conduct assurance audits across our SBUs, which are essential for maintaining and improving governance, risk management, and internal controls. They also ensure accountability to the Board of Directors and shareholders. Annually, the Internal Audit Department develops a comprehensive audit plan, which outlines regular, thorough audits to identify significant risks. These risks are reported to the Audit Committee and relevant management for timely action. In 2024, we finalized all twelve internal audit engagements. In line with best practices, Internal Audit functionally reports to the Audit Committee and administratively to the CEO. The department has full and unrestricted access to all records, physical properties, and personnel within TASNEE and its affiliates, essential for performing its audits. Beyond auditing, the department also conducts internal assessments as part of the Quality Assurance and Improvement Program in conformance with the International Standards for the Professional Practice of Internal Auditing set by the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA). As part of the Quality Assurance and Improvement Program, and in line with IIA standards, the department underwent an independent External Quality Assessment conducted by the Saudi Institute of Internal Auditors. This assessment was conducted in alignment with the International Professional Practices Framework (IPPF) standards. The Internal Audit department has achieved the rating of 'General Conformance', which is the highest level of conformance awarded by the Saudi Institute of Internal Auditors. This achievement underscores our commitment to excellence, professionalism, and adherence to the best globally recognized practices in internal auditing. Throughout the year, all activities were carried out in accordance with the risk-based audit plan approved by the Audit Committee, focusing on high-risk areas to support our goals and protect our assets. The audit process evaluates the efficiency and effectiveness of internal controls. Results are shared with the relevant departments and SBUs to address findings, implement corrective actions, and ensure completion within agreed timeframes. Regular status reports highlight achievements, challenges, and the risks associated with unresolved observations and recommendations.

TASNEE is deeply committed to protecting, respecting, and promoting human rights across all aspects of our operations. We adhere to international human rights standards, such as those outlined by the United Nations, and actively engage with experts, clients, and industry peers to identify and address any actual or potential human rights concerns within our value chain. Our commitment ensures that we comply with all relevant laws to protect and uphold human rights. Our Code of Conduct explicitly incorporates human rights, setting clear expectations not only for our employees but also for our suppliers. We require our suppliers to uphold the highest standards by implementing robust operational procedures and mechanisms to safeguard human rights. Human rights are also embedded in our employment application documents, ensuring that every employee complies with these principles from their very first day with us.

content_text: Customer satisfaction is fundamental to our business success. We have consistently worked to establish a strong reputation as a reliable and trustworthy service provider, earning the confidence of our clients. While complaints are inevitable for a company of our size, we have a dedicated team of skilled customer service professionals who are trained to handle them efficiently. Each complaint is carefully tracked throughout the process, with a focus on addressing concerns and resolving issues at the earliest opportunity. We also analyze the root causes of complaints to ensure they do not recur. The feedback we receive help guide continuous improvements in our processes and systems, maintaining high standards. Our customer service team is proactive, regularly conducting on-site visits to manage key accounts, offering support, and gathering additional feedback. In the event of a serious complaint, our structured governance and reporting system ensures that senior management is informed promptly, enabling them to take appropriate action. In 2024, the number of customer complaints received by Downstream increased by 83 compared to the previous year's complaints, representing a 27.7% rise. To address such complaints, several measures have been put in place, such as increasing daily quality checkpoints, extending aging time for specific stock-keeping units, and monitoring film production parameters more thoroughly to improve overall product quality and reduce complaints. Notably, no substantiated complaints were received concerning breaches of customer privacy or data loss, continuing the trend of secure and reliable service with no reported incidents in these areas.

TASNEE Corporate Cybersecurity Capability Maturity Model Integration (CMMI) score stands at 3.7 out of 5. This score is higher than the global (2.7) and Saudi Arabia (3.4) averages. In 2024 we released a comprehensive set of cybersecurity policies for IT (Information Technology) and OT (Operational Technology). It covered all regulatory requirements in addition to what is required to support business initiatives such as Artificial Intelligence (AI). We achieved several key milestones, including the successful segregation of TASNEE Petrochemical SBU network to enhance cybersecurity. Minimizing cyber risks from certain scenarios such as worm malware infection where it was possible to propagate quickly through the various nodes in the network. Additionally, we developed and integrated a comprehensive OT incident response preparation to ensure swift and effective action in the event of a cybersecurity incident by conducting continuous monitoring and availing internal and external incident response teams. To further improve our cybersecurity management processes, we launched an Enterprise Governance, Risk, and Compliance (EGRC) system application. This demonstrates our ongoing commitment to advancing our cybersecurity capabilities, aligning with industry best practices, and ensuring robust security measures across the organization.

Technology and Innovation at TASNEE is driven by our T&I Center in Jubail, which provides critical research and development, along with technical assistance to support product development and operations across the company. The center focuses on four key areas: research and development, testing, training, and technical support. The labs are ISO/IEC 17025:2017-accredited by the International Accreditation Service (IAS), and the Saudi Accreditation Committee (SAC), with the accreditation renewed in 2023. The T&I Center plays a central role in driving innovation and operational excellence at TASNEE. It leads to key initiatives in energy efficiency technologies, product development, process optimization, and manufacturing enhancements, all of which contribute to ESG and Sustainability and business growth. As one of the best-equipped research and development centers in petrochemical and plastic processing, the T&I division leverages cutting-edge technology and expertise to accelerate business development, ensuring we remain competitive and responsive to industry advancements, while delivering highquality products and technical services. T&I continuously focuses on product and process development to improve profitability and efficiency. This includes creating new injection molding grades, eliminating transition grades, and advancing high-tenacity fiber production. Additionally, we have achieved cost optimization through masterbatch and additive improvements for downstream products such as Agri-film and pipe solutions. These efforts support TASNEE local content strategy, fostering business continuity and customer-driven innovation. Additionally, strategic projects on sustainable product development, including gas storage materials and plastic chemical recycling, highlight our commitment to circular economy principles. content_text: The subject matter for our limited assurance engagement included the selected quantitative indicators outlined below: -  Water Management -  Green House Gas (GHG) Accounting -  Waste Management As presented in the Company's 2024 Sustainability Report for the year ended 31 December 2024, which was prepared and presented by the Company's management. The criteria for this limited assurance engagement were the reporting requirements of the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) standards issued by the Global Sustainability Standards Board (GSSB). The applicable criteria for each selected indicator can be found in Annexure 1 of this report.

The assurance process was conducted in line with the requirements of the International Standard on Assurance Engagements-lSAE 3000 Revised, Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information and International Standard on Assurance Engagements- ISAE 3410, Assurance Engagements on Greenhouse Gas Statements.

Our assurance was primarily based on Company-provided documentation and interactions with relevant personnel. Our engagement, conducted on a test basis; additionally, our procedures did not encompass testing the completeness of outputs from the Company's data collecting systems, used for the compilation of the Subject Matter information. The Subject Matter may contain errors or irregularities that remain undetected due to limitations. Additionally, for the purpose of this limited assurance engagement, we have not performed any procedures involving: -  Verifying any assertions or qualitative information within the ESG report beyond the quantitative data relating to the specified indicators mentioned in the subject matter. -  Evaluating the accuracy and completeness of the reporting boundaries defined by the management for the purpose of the ESG report. -  Reviewing the method utilized by management to conduct materiality assessment. -  Company position statements (including any expression of opinion, belief, aspiration, expectation, aim or future intent). -  Historic text which was unchanged from previous years and did not relate to ongoing activities. -  Financial data. -  Appropriateness of commitments and objectives chosen by the company.
